requirements_slice.system_goal: Rerun the existing compact Day/home DEV chip diagnostics disclosure through bounded frontend verification and packet-local evidence without changing DayBrief contracts, backend traffic, or production behavior

in_scope.item: Reuse the existing Day/home dev/prod chip on `/` as the only runtime-disclosure entry point.
Keep the collapsed DEV chip visually compact and local to the Day hero area.
In non-production only, expand and collapse a local disclosure that shows render path, bootstrap result, and current mode from existing client state.
Re-run the targeted unit, Playwright, visual, and packet-local read-only observability lanes through the live pipeline.
Publish Prefect artifacts for the rerun wave so verifier, reviewer, and architect evidence is inspectable.

out_of_scope.item: Any new payload field, scoring change, explainability change, or business-logic change.
Any new top-level banner, separate diagnostics screen, or Week or other-surface expansion.
Any diagnostics field beyond render path, bootstrap result, and current mode.
Any new slice definition separate from the existing Day dev-indicator slice.
Any canonical Today/Week closeout claim or runtime emitter ownership from this frontend-only helper wave.

use_case.summary: Re-run the existing Day runtime disclosure slice and verify both product behavior and evidence publication.
use_case.scenario: On `/` in non-production, tapping the compact chip expands a local disclosure with render path, bootstrap result, and runtime mode.
Tapping the chip again collapses the disclosure and restores the compact local state.
In production and on non-home routes, the chip remains visually unchanged and inert and no diagnostics block appears.
The live rerun publishes verifier, reviewer, and architect evidence artifacts and records an explicit packet-local read-only observability verdict.

business_invariants.invariant: The disclosure is client-local helper UI only and must not add backend requests or payload fields.
Only render path, bootstrap result, and current mode may appear in the visible disclosure body.
Interactive behavior is limited to non-production on `/`.
Production behavior and non-home routes remain inert and visually unchanged.
DayBrief hero, domains, CTA, scoring, readiness semantics, and backend behavior remain unchanged.
The rerun reuses the existing Day dev-indicator slice and must not broaden it into a new diagnostics surface.
Evidence ownership for this frontend-only helper wave is packet_local only; no canonical_flow_commands are owned here.

expected_failure_handling.item: If any diagnostics source is absent, render a stable unknown or unavailable value instead of blocking the Day screen.
If the shell-owned badge leaks interaction outside `/`, stop and route to rework rather than widening the feature.
If the implementation causes a crash, hydration issue, or 500, add or update the smallest reproduction test before claiming green.
If packet-local evidence lacks canonical Today/Week emission, the verdict may be degraded-but-expected when local visual, command, and read-only evidence remain attributable.
If packet-local evidence is missing entirely or shows unexpected Day degradation, the wave remains blocked and cannot be accepted.
If no dedicated production Playwright host is available, deterministic unit proof is the minimum acceptable production-inert lane.

known_defects.defect: The prior verifier closeout over-required canonical Today/Week evidence for a frontend-only helper; this rerun closes packet-local evidence without redesigning the slice or claiming canonical runtime emission.
Production visual proof depends on deterministic unit coverage when the active Playwright stack only exercises the non-production frontend.

success_criteria.criterion: The Day chip stays compact in collapsed state.
In non-production on `/`, tapping the chip expands and collapses a local disclosure.
The disclosure shows render path, bootstrap result, and current mode only.
Production and non-home routes stay visually and behaviorally unchanged.
Verifier evidence includes dev-collapsed, dev-expanded, and prod-inert proof.
Packet-local read-only observability verdict is explicit, classified as clean or degraded-but-expected, and shows no unexpected Day degradation.
Prefect artifacts are published for the rerun coder, verifier, reviewer, and architect packet chain.
